topics.label: Lecture Introduction and the Hallmarks of Cancer Framework
topics.groupedBecause: This topic frames the lecture by outlining learning outcomes, introducing the multistep tumor progression model, and establishing the hallmarks of cancer framework.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Evasion of Growth Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling cascades including Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinases, and TGF-beta enable cancer cells to sustain proliferation and evade growth inhibition.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Cancer Cells
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells become arrested in an undifferentiated progenitor state, using examples from hematological malignancies and colorectal crypts.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of mitochondrial Bax and BCL2 proteins.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Senescence, and Mutation-Driven Hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells bypass telomere shortening and p53-mediated senescence to achieve immortalization, concluding the survey of direct mutation-driven hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic Reprogramming in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells alter their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations to satisfy biosynthetic demands and modify the epigenome.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the requirement for tumor angiogenesis, its onset during progression, and how the balance of angiogenic activators and inhibitors controls new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Clinical Detection of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the metastatic cascade, methods for detecting circulating and nodal tumor cells, and the clonal and genomic characteristics of metastases.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Hallmark Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic closes the lecture by reviewing the convergence of cancer hallmarks, discussing recent literature expansions, and providing concluding housekeeping instructions.
